Your First Weeks Managing a Team

Open this when you have just started leading people, perhaps the ones who were your peers last month, and you are unsure what the job actually is. It gives you a few first moves that build trust before you change anything.

Managing People · Work · Communication · Assertiveness · 8 items · once a week

The checklist

  • Ask each person what they need from you — The answers are more useful than any plan you arrive with.
  • Change nothing in the first two weeks — Listening first buys you the credit to change things later.
  • Book a short regular time with each one — A standing slot beats an open door nobody walks through.
  • Say out loud what you will decide alone — Clear lines stop people guessing where their say ends.
  • Pass on the credit by name — Naming who did what costs you nothing and buys a great deal.
  • Give awkward feedback early and small — A quiet word in week one saves a hard talk in month three.
  • Find your own place to complain — Your team is not where your frustration goes.
  • Protect one block for your own work — A calendar of nothing but meetings is how new managers drown.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it once a week, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
